close_reason: Landed paired with .20. New AuthHeader<'a> opaque wrapper with manual Debug redacting the value bytes to '[REDACTED]'. The credential is reachable only via the explicit expose_value() accessor; the call-site name is the visible signal in code review against a future tracing::*-formatter leak. Canary regression test asserts the wrapper Debug never contains the canary literal.
description:
Section A — Key Material Lifecycle (compile-time tagging).

AuthProvider::auth_header at crate-jmap-base-client/src/auth.rs:112-139 returns Option<(&str, &str)> — a plain string tuple. The trait rustdoc at lines 100-102 carries a verbal contract:

  'Implementations must not log the return value of auth_header; it contains credentials.'

This contract is documentation-only. A custom AuthProvider implementor (kith, stoa, third-party consumer) can compile a tracing::info!(header = ?self.auth_header(), ...) call without any warning. The workspace AGENTS.md 'Security testing' section anticipated this and prescribed the Debug + log-capture canary tripwires for the SHIPPED implementations (BearerAuth, BasicAuth, NoneAuth). The tripwires do not transit through to third-party implementations.

The workspace-wide rule from /review-crypto-security Section A is more strict: 'In Rust, prefer wrappers that gate access (secrecy::Secret<T>, zeroize::Zeroizing<T>).'

# What goes wrong

A future *-client extension crate or a downstream consumer implements a custom AuthProvider (e.g., OAuth refresh token, session-cookie auth, mTLS-bound session) and writes a normal-looking debug log:

```rust
impl AuthProvider for OAuthRefresh {
    fn auth_header(&self) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
        tracing::debug!("injecting auth"); // OK
        let hdr = ("authorization", self.current_bearer.as_str());
        tracing::trace!(?hdr, "injecting auth"); // SILENT LEAK
        Some(hdr)
    }
}
```

The credential leaks via Debug-formatted args. No compile-time signal. No test in this crate catches it.

# Suggested fix (forward-major-version)

Migrate AuthProvider::auth_header to return a typed secret wrapper. Options:

1) Newtype owned by this crate:

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct AuthHeader<'a> {
    name: &'a str,
    value: &'a str, // exposed only via .value() with a 'do not log' doc
}

impl fmt::Debug for AuthHeader<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("AuthHeader").field("name", &self.name).field("value", &"[REDACTED]").finish()
    }
}

trait AuthProvider {
    fn auth_header(&self) -> Option<AuthHeader<'_>>;
}
```

This is a SemVer-break for the trait signature; defer to the next major.

2) Add the secrecy crate dependency and return Option<(&str, SecretSlice<u8>)> or similar. Heavier.

3) Document the constraint more loudly and add a doctest example that demonstrates the discipline. Cheap, but does not prevent the leak.

# Why this is opinion, not bug

The contract is documented; the SHIPPED implementations are tripwired. The defect window is in HYPOTHETICAL third-party implementations. The fix is a major-version breaking change. P3 with the opinion label, surfaced for completeness; if the workspace's next-major plan does not include AuthProvider reshape, close as wontfix.

# Cross-reference

This finding is the security-side companion to the JMAP-6r7c.20 finding ('AuthProvider::auth_header signature locks header into single static pair'). Both call for a major-version reshape of the same method. Address them together when the next major lands.
